title: Counter Standard: Handing Over Equipment Rental and Demo Kit and Drawing Rental Days
content:
## Who the kit goes to

Kit is handed over only to the rider it was fitted for or to the adult who opened the agreement on their behalf.

## What must stand on the agreement first

Kit is handed over only when the rider's signed liability release is recorded against the agreement, and where the package calls for it, only when a photographic identity document has been seen at the counter.

The release is a matter of the record: what counts is that the rider's signed release stands recorded against that one agreement, read before the kit leaves the counter, and not that the guest says the release was signed. Each package of the Equipment Rental and Demo line records for itself whether a photographic identity document is called for at the counter.

## The binding release setting

The binding release setting is worked from the rider's height, weight, age and ability as recorded on the agreement, and a technician resets it whenever any of those is corrected; a rider who tells the shop a different weight after collection has the kit reset rather than the record quietly changed.

## Drawing rental days

One rental day is drawn for each date the kit is out, counted from the date of collection through the date of hand-in inclusive, so kit collected in the afternoon and handed in the next morning has used two days.

Days are not drawn for dates before collection even where the reservation covered them, and the days a guest does not ski are not given back.

### The count on hypothetical dates

| Collected | Handed in | Dates the kit was out | Rental days drawn |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 14 January, afternoon | 15 January, morning | 14 and 15 January | 2 |
| 14 January | 14 January | 14 January | 1 |
| 14 January, on a reservation written from 12 January | 16 January | 14, 15 and 16 January | 3 |
| 14 January, with no skiing on 15 January | 16 January | 14, 15 and 16 January | 3 |

The third row shows the dates before collection dropping out of the count although the reservation covered them; the fourth shows the day the guest did not ski staying in it.

## Points of judgement

**An adult collecting for a child.** Kit fitted for a child goes to that child or to the adult who opened the agreement on the child's behalf.

**A guest who gives a different weight after collection.** The kit is reset by a technician against the corrected figure; the agreement is not simply amended behind the counter, and the reset follows every correction to the rider's height, weight, age or ability.
